key_insight: Accurate PDE predictions do not guarantee accurate responses to small input changes. TangentPDE targets both by using sparse finite-difference supervision to teach neural operators how solutions vary locally.
problem_solved: Training primarily on state reconstruction constrains predictions at observed inputs but can leave local sensitivity poorly characterized.
method: Use finite differences to approximate directional derivatives of the PDE solution operator.
Construct task-relevant, finite-step perturbations to characterize local input–output responses.
Use sparse supervision of these responses to guide learning beyond state prediction alone.
impact: Learning local responses could make neural PDE operators more useful for sensitivity analysis and optimization, where how predictions change matters as much as their values. The provided abstract excerpt does not report quantitative results.
visual_elements: Side-by-side curves: two models match an observed solution but respond differently to nearby inputs.
Perturbation diagram: input → small directional change → corresponding solution change.
Finite-difference illustration: two nearby evaluations approximate a directional derivative.
Training schematic contrasting state-only supervision with state-plus-local-response supervision.
paper_title: TangentPDE: Learning Local Operator Responses with Sparse Finite-Difference Supervision
paper_authors: Xinjian Xie, Ruxuan Chen, Jiashu Li, Tianyu Gao, Ye Wei
